small_guidance:
- Add larger GEMM tile configs sized to M=1024, N=8192, K=8192: try `BLOCK_M=128/256, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64` with `num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4`, and include a `GROUP_M=8` block-swizzle (use a 2D-flattened grid with row-group reordering) to improve L2 reuse across N tiles.
- Switch the single-pass softmax path to use larger `BLOCK_N` (N=8192 fits in 8192-wide block with num_warps=16 or use 2-pass with BLOCK_N=4096, num_warps=8, num_stages=2) — currently N=8192 falls into the tiled 3-pass path which reloads x 3×; a 2-pass online softmax avoids one reload.
- Cache `Wt` once in `__init__` (or lazily on first forward) instead of checking `_version` every call, and store the fused BN scale/bias as buffers updated only when running stats change, to remove per-call host-side tensor construction overhead.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into the GEMM epilogue via a split-K-free streaming design: launch one program per row-tile spanning the full N (persistent across N tiles), accumulate the full row, then do online-softmax max/sum and normalize in registers/SMEM before storing — eliminates the separate softmax kernel and its two extra reads of the 1024×8192 intermediate (~32MB).
- Alternatively, use a two-kernel design where GEMM stores to the intermediate while computing per-row running max and partial sum into auxiliary buffers (one program per (row, N-tile)), then a tiny normalize kernel divides — this avoids the full extra max-pass over N=8192.
- Consider FP16/BF16 accumulation path: cast x and Wt to bf16 for `tl.dot` on Ada (RTX 4090 has strong bf16 tensor cores), keep fp32 accumulator and epilogue — the 8192×8192 GEMM is the dominant cost and bf16 tensor cores roughly double throughput vs tf32.
